_comment: RFC-0001 slice B3a fixture: fetch-config + provenance stub for tests/corpus. Each entry under 'corpus' is {version, source, prepare?} -- the same shape RFC-0001 SS B.3's compat-manifest 'corpus' array records for provenance ({"version": ..., "source": "git:owner/repo@<sha>"}). 'source' is a well-formed but FAKE git:owner/repo@<40-hex-sha> placeholder -- this fixture corpus is hand-authored, never actually fetched. 'prepare' (present on exactly ONE entry here, 2.0.0) is RESERVED, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: the harvester (tools/harvest/harvester.nim's loadCorpusProvenance) reads only 'version' and 'source' from this file and silently ignores 'prepare' and '_comment' -- no fetch script or hook currently runs it. It documents the intended shape of a future optional shell command that would run BEFORE a version's header snapshot is captured, for libraries whose public headers are configure/generate outputs rather than checked-in files (mbedtls's config-dependent headers are RFC-0001 SS B.2's motivating case). It's attached to one entry purely so slice B3's harvester (and any real fetch script modeled on this file) has a concrete example of the field's intended shape to target once wired up. See tests/corpus/README.md for the full classification narrative this corpus exists to exercise.
